nodes.description: Random-walk trails claim grid cells rendered as solid/chequered/fives motifs, then unclaimed cells fill with hatching and nodes shift
nodes.notable: three-phase run: stepping trails, then filling empty space with hatch lines, then shifting nodes

nodes.name: grid
nodes.description: Greedy subdivision of a small grid into rectangular regions, each clip-filled with animated sliding black-and-white stripes by orientation
nodes.notable: stripe direction picked per region from its aspect ratio; stripes slide with playhead

nodes.name: arcs
nodes.description: Quarter-circle Wang-style tiles grow into areas via edge-matching random walk on a 3x3 grid, filled from found palettes
nodes.notable: cell types constrained by an edge-mirror table so arcs stay continuous across shared edges

nodes.name: arcs-reduction
nodes.description: Arc Wang tiles on a 4x3 grid grown as areas, then a reduction pass recolors isolated cells to their dominant edge-aware neighbour
nodes.notable: edge-aware reduction only counts a neighbour's color if its shared edge is closed

nodes.name: arcs-reduction-gen-color
nodes.description: Arc Wang tiles on a 3x3 grid with a color-reduction pass, colors picked from found palettes filtered for mutual WCAG contrast
nodes.notable: background and inks chosen by luminance and pairwise contrast thresholds; regenerates every 60 frames

nodes.name: arcs-reduction-rounded
nodes.description: Arc Wang tiles with color reduction, rounded corners on open ends and bg-colored corner notches carving smooth quilt-like shapes
nodes.notable: corner rounding derived from open/closed edges of neighbours; blank cells drop out to background

nodes.name: arcs-reduction-rounded-animated
nodes.description: Precomputed rounded arc-tile shapes cross-fade via directional slide transitions; changed cells slide in/out as unioned fills, seamless loop
nodes.notable: abutting cells merged into one path per fill to avoid antialiased seams; tweakpane controls shape count and transition

nodes.name: everything
nodes.description: Full Wang-tile set (right triangles plus quarter-arc corners) grown into edge-matched areas on a 3x3 grid from found palettes
nodes.notable: widest tile vocabulary of the series: nine cell types combining flat, triangular and arc edges

nodes.name: grid-areas
nodes.description: Right-triangle and square Wang tiles grown into edge-matched areas on a 3x3 grid, each area one found-palette color
nodes.notable: triangle-only tile set; areas grow by matching filled edges between neighbours

nodes.name: grid-areas-process
nodes.description: Same triangle Wang-tile area filler animated as a white-on-black progressive reveal cell by cell with debug indices and grid overlay
nodes.notable: debug-view aesthetic: exposes the generation order with numbered cells and magenta grid lines

nodes.name: grid-areas-process-2
nodes.description: Triangle Wang-tile areas revealed area by area along the playhead, colored from found palettes with a debug grid and indices
nodes.notable: reveals whole areas at a time rather than single cells, showing the region structure emerging

nodes.name: just-arcs
nodes.description: Only the four quarter-arc Wang tiles grown into edge-matched areas on a 3x3 grid, each area a found-palette color
nodes.notable: pared-back arc-only variant; areas can start from any arc type rather than a full square

nodes.name: patchwork
nodes.description: 50k points in a triangle repeatedly k-means clustered, least-dense cluster hulled and removed, hulls tinted by an oklch hue ramp
nodes.notable: iterative peel: each pass carves off the sparsest cluster as a convex-hull patch until points run out

nodes.name: patchwork-full
nodes.description: Triangle grid where each cell is fractured by k-means/convex-hull into palette-colored patches, then Atkinson-dithered
nodes.notable: tiles a triangular lattice then shatters each triangle into hull patches; downscaled Atkinson dither for a grainy print look

nodes.name: pd-timeline-example
nodes.description: A single square eased around the canvas perimeter using @daeinc/pd-timeline sequential ranges (left-right, top-bottom, etc.)
nodes.notable: demo of the pd-timeline range API sequencing four directional moves into one loop

nodes.name: penplot-example
nodes.description: Plotter artwork of 30 concentric circles plus 12 crosshatch diameters, exported to optimized SVG at A4 physical dimensions
nodes.notable: penplot export scaffold: builds paths in cm and renders an optimized plotter SVG

nodes.name: perspectives
nodes.description: One-point-perspective corridor: radial lines to a central vanishing point with concentric quad panels colored from a rampensau ramp
nodes.notable: nested inner/outer rings of angled vertices form trapezoidal wall panels around the vanishing point

nodes.name: basic
nodes.description: Physarum slime-mold simulation: 16k agents sense trail brightness ahead/left/right, steer and wrap, leaving white paths on fading black
nodes.notable: reads back canvas pixels each frame as the pheromone field driving agent turning

nodes.name: circles
nodes.description: Physarum slime-mold simulation seeded on two rings so networks grow outward from circular emitters into white trail structures
nodes.notable: agents spawned on two offset circles rather than uniformly, giving two competing colonies

nodes.name: offscreen
nodes.description: Physarum agents spawned on sphere-packed circles; trails accumulate in an offscreen pheromone buffer while colored dots render on-screen, mouse-seedable, optional dither
nodes.notable: separates the sensed trail field (offscreen) from the colored display; drag to inject agents, 'd' toggles Atkinson dither

nodes.name: packed-circles
nodes.description: Physarum/slime-mold agents seeded on the rims of packed circles, steering by sensing white trails; faint white marks on black
nodes.notable: Agents read the canvas back via getImageData each frame, so the drawn trails become the sensor field.

nodes.name: trail
nodes.description: Physarum agents seeded on packed circles leave gradient trails colored per-agent; sensing runs on an offscreen buffer, optional Atkinson dither
nodes.notable: Separates a hidden trail-sensing buffer from the visible gradient-stroke render; palette drawn from mindful + auto-albers sets.

nodes.name: pixel-flow
nodes.description: A 100x100 grid of colored cells that migrate along noise-chosen 8-neighbor directions each frame, wrapping at the edges

nodes.name: pixel-noise
nodes.description: A 100x100 grid where each cell samples a color index from an animated 3D value-noise field, producing drifting color regions

nodes.name: pro-color
nodes.description: Recursively subdivided horizontal bands (each block split again into sub-blocks) after a Haus Konstruktiv concrete-art work; palette recomposes every 30 frames
nodes.notable: After 'Quanten-Aequivalenz an der Horizontalen II'; oklch triadic palettes from pro-color-harmonies.

nodes.name: pro-color-shift
nodes.description: Same recursive band layout as pro-color, but each rectangle clips a vertically scrolling three-tone gradient so the blocks appear to shift
nodes.notable: lerpFrames drives per-rect offsets under a clip, giving a seamless looping vertical scroll within the static grid.

nodes.name: rybitten
nodes.description: The recursive quantum-equivalence band layout colored from RYB color-mixing cubes (Itten, Goethe, Munsell, etc.); recomposes every 30 frames
nodes.notable: Picks a random historical RYB gamut cube from rybitten so hue relationships follow painterly color wheels, not RGB.

nodes.name: rybitten-monochrome-rainbow
nodes.description: Quantum-equivalence band layout filled from a hand-built monochrome RYB cube swept through a full hue rainbow via t-parameterized color functions
nodes.notable: Custom 8-entry ColorCube tuned to a near-monochrome ramp, then hue-cycled to read as a tonal rainbow.

nodes.name: rybitten-rainbow
nodes.description: Quantum-equivalence band layout with colors from a random RYB gamut cube swept through 360-degree hue via t-parameterized color functions

nodes.name: rybitten-rgb-rainbow
nodes.description: Quantum-equivalence band layout using procedurally built RGB-biased RYB cubes (one channel ramped), hue-cycled across a rainbow
nodes.notable: Cubes are synthesized by ramping one of R/G/B while fixing the others, biasing the whole RYB mix toward a channel.

nodes.name: quine
nodes.description: A self-reproducing sketch: it stores its own source and scrolls that text as an infinite carousel of monospace code lines on near-black
nodes.notable: A true quine — the string reprints itself via PLACEHOLDER escaping, and the image is literally its own code.

nodes.name: basic
nodes.description: 2D raycasting: a mouse-following point emits 360 rays that terminate on random wall segments, drawn as white light rays on black

nodes.name: circles
nodes.description: Raycast visibility among packed circles: the lit polygon is cut out of a black shadow layer with destination-out so light reveals the ground

nodes.name: grid
nodes.description: Raycast light/shadow over a grid of rounded rectangles and circles; the emitter tracks diagonally across the canvas, lit area in bg color over fg shadow
nodes.notable: 720 rays sorted by angle build a smooth visibility polygon; WCAG-contrast filtering picks the fg/light colors.

nodes.name: solid
nodes.description: 2D raycasting against random wall segments, filling the mouse-lit region as a solid translucent visibility polygon on black

nodes.name: base
nodes.description: A colored field cut by a black stepped-polygon shape whose vertices tween between random target configurations; portrait format
nodes.notable: Two-color (fg/bg) oklch pair from one random hue; the composition is a single morphing negative-space silhouette.

nodes.name: spring
nodes.description: The red-and-black stepped silhouette animated with per-vertex spring physics toward cycling target shapes, giving overshoot and settle

nodes.name: spring-anticipation
nodes.description: The red-and-black spring silhouette with added anticipation — vertices pull back before lunging toward each new target shape
nodes.notable: Adds an anticipation phase to the spring so motion has a cartoon wind-up before the snap.

nodes.name: haberdashery
nodes.description: Packed circles wrapped by one continuous rubber band with convex/concave/floater pegs, rendered as a beveled tube with an animated dashed conveyor
nodes.notable: Cheapest-insertion + 2-opt build a non-self-crossing contact cycle; role-aware tangents let the band dip into concave dents. Tweakpane controls.

nodes.name: rubber-band-stipple
nodes.description: Drifting poisson-disc circles paired by tangent 'rubber band' outlines; each circle filled by a noise-mapped color with a bg inner dot
nodes.notable: Rubber bands are tangent-line-plus-arc wraps between circle pairs; edges assigned greedily to avoid chain topology.

nodes.name: shape
nodes.description: Nested rubber-band hull outlines: several independent poisson-disc circle layers, each wrapped by its drifting convex-hull membrane
nodes.notable: Up to 12 pre-generated layers stay stable when the layer slider changes; each is an independent hull outline. Tweakpane controls.

nodes.name: shapes
nodes.description: Denser variant of rubber-band-stipple: drifting poisson-disc circles with many tangent rubber-band links (no orphan circles) plus stipple fills
nodes.notable: Higher connection distance plus an orphan-fixup pass yields a woven web rather than isolated pairs.

nodes.name: skeleton-albers
nodes.description: A hull-boundary membrane with interior circles tied to it by tendon edges, layered with stepped lightness/hue color shifts
nodes.notable: Interior nodes connect to hull-boundary nodes like a skeleton; per-layer lightness+hue steps nod to Albers color studies. Tweakpane controls.

nodes.name: skeleton-clusters
nodes.description: Multiple clustered skeletons: circles grouped into 2-4 clusters, each with its own hull membrane and interior tendon edges, beveled
nodes.notable: Positions are partitioned into clusters, each getting a stable boundary hull and its own tendon graph. Tweakpane controls.

nodes.name: skeleton-field
nodes.description: Noise-sized discs packed and relaxed, wrapped by a rubber-band convex hull filled with a rotating linear gradient; discs carry radial gradients.
nodes.notable: Rubber-band hull (external tangents + arcs of a disk cluster) filled by a linear gradient whose angle rotates once per loop.

nodes.name: skeleton-grid
nodes.description: Grid of noise-perturbed circles wrapped by a rubber-band hull, linked by 'tendon' bands along rook adjacency; beveled discs with center dots.
nodes.notable: Deterministic per-cell perturbation; tendons follow the grid's 4-connectivity adjacency.

nodes.name: skeleton-inverted
nodes.description: Figure/ground inversion: a solid color field with the rubber-band hull cut out as a negative shape; tendons extend the cut; clean gradient discs.
nodes.notable: The hull and tendons are filled with the void color so they read as carved out of a solid field.

nodes.name: skeleton-line
nodes.description: Line-only variant: concentric rubber-band hull layers, concentric ring tendons, and concentric rings inside each circle over a max-contrast pair.
nodes.notable: Palette reduced to the highest-WCAG-contrast pair; everything drawn as concentric line contours, no fills.

nodes.name: skeleton-shape
nodes.description: Canonical variant: noise-sized discs wrapped by a rubber-band hull, tendon bands to boundary, and 'stipple' beveled discs with lit center dots.
nodes.notable: The archetype of the series: bevel-gradient discs with a beveled center dot under a single overhead-left light.

nodes.name: skeleton-singular
nodes.description: Few large noise-driven discs wrapped by a rubber-band hull filled with a rotating linear gradient; reads as one amoeboid form.
nodes.notable: Wider margins and larger radii keep the hull from collapsing so a handful of discs merge into a single silhouette.

nodes.name: tendon-albers
nodes.description: MST-linked discs joined by nested rubber-band 'tendon' bands, each ring lightness- and hue-shifted like a layered Albers color study.
nodes.notable: Prim's MST gives minimal-length tendons; concentric bands step lightness/hue for an Interaction-of-Color effect.

nodes.name: weaving-techniques
nodes.description: Pulley/rope schematic: cross-hatched discs hung by strands that wrap tangentially over a master pulley, with rubber-band cross-bracing.
nodes.notable: Technical-drawing register: paper/ink two-tone, tangent strands wrapping a master pulley, hatched discs with anchor tabs.

nodes.name: wrap
nodes.description: Rubber band with convex, concave 'dent', and floater pegs; role-aware tangents, cheapest-insertion + 2-opt to avoid crossings, beveled tube stroke.
nodes.notable: Most elaborate of the family: concave dents pull the band inward, floaters auto-insert on crossing, 2-opt removes self-crossings; geometry precomputed (no motion).

nodes.name: basic
nodes.description: Minimal study: a rubber band wraps three white discs picked from a 3x3 grid, drawn behind them on near-black.
nodes.notable: The seed of the rubber-band series: tangent-line + arc band around three hull discs.

nodes.name: micro-graphics
nodes.description: Rubber-band diagram framed as a mock technical UI: gear/asterisk/ring glyph discs, a Devanagari label, frame counter, and animated bar meters.
nodes.notable: Landscape HUD-style composition: rotating gear/asterisk glyphs and sine-driven pill bars around the rubber-band motif.

nodes.name: shatter
nodes.description: An equilateral triangle k-means-clustered into convex-hull shards that explode outward with rotation on a keyframed timeline; optional Atkinson dither.
nodes.notable: Curtains reveal the triangle, then it fractures via k-means/convex-hull and each shard flies out sized by its area.

nodes.name: no-250
nodes.description: Two sliding rectangle clusters (base/extension/accent) over a colored column-row grid; overlaps drawn white, triple-overlaps grey; piston-eased motion.
nodes.notable: Neighbor-aware coloring of the background grid; overlap/triple-overlap regions recomputed each frame as the clusters slide.

nodes.name: no-251
nodes.description: Sibling of no-250 stripped to intersections only: overlapping black rectangles on black, visible solely where they overlap (white) or triple-overlap (grey).
nodes.notable: Forms exist only as their overlaps — the rectangles themselves vanish into the black ground.

nodes.name: slashes
nodes.description: Random point clouds in stacked rectangular domains reduced to nested convex-hull polygons, tinted by rampensau hue ramps on a light ground.
nodes.notable: Same k-means/convex-hull decomposition as shatter but held static and layered per-domain like torn paper.

nodes.name: 16x16
nodes.description: 4x4 tiling of 16x16 dot grids where color index = floor(dist^scale) mod palette; each tile uses a different scale exponent; hues rotate over the loop.
nodes.notable: Concentric-square banding from a distance-power-modulo rule, retiled at escalating scale factors.

nodes.name: snowflake
nodes.description: Single 40x40 dot grid with concentric-square color banding via floor(dist^scale) mod palette; scale factor slowly drifts. Dots or split X/dot mode.
nodes.notable: The base version of the distance-power-modulo color-banding idea, over one grid with a creeping scale exponent.

nodes.name: rug
nodes.description: Packed verlet soft-bodies (double concentric spring rings) jostle via quadtree collision, then Chaikin-smoothed into a rug of colored blobs.
nodes.notable: Soft bodies settle under gravity then, past playhead 0.8, freeze and heavily Chaikin-smooth into rounded fabric-like shapes.

nodes.name: verlet-101
nodes.description: Teaching sketch: verlet ring meshes with a central nucleus spring, packed as circles, drawn as visible particles, springs, and outline on white.
nodes.notable: Exposes the spring topology (neighbor + nucleus springs, per-particle attraction) rather than hiding it in a fill.

nodes.name: verlet-collision
nodes.description: Verlet soft-bodies with brute-force O(n^2) inter-body collision, drawn as filled black silhouettes on white under gravity.
nodes.notable: The naive collision step (every particle vs every other) that the quadtree sibling optimizes.

nodes.name: verlet-collision-quadtree
nodes.description: Quadtree-accelerated verlet collision study: packed soft-bodies with double concentric spring rings settle into filled black blobs on a framed ground.
nodes.notable: Radius-query quadtree replaces the O(n^2) neighbor scan; bodies have inner + outer spring rings for firmer shells.

nodes.name: rybitten-blinds
nodes.description: 40x40 grid of squares colored in a RYB color model, placed by weighted chance from a 5-hue-step palette with a heavy weight toward near-black.
nodes.notable: Uses the rybitten RYB cubes for painterly hue mixing; the folder name echoes Kelly's chance spectrum grids.

nodes.name: stipling-noise
nodes.description: Weighted Voronoi stippling: points relax toward noise-weighted centroids then back over the loop; cells stroked, colored dots sized by local weight.
nodes.notable: Points seeded only where noise is high, migrate to weighted centroids and return; dot diameter encodes cell weight with a bg center hole.

nodes.name: voronoi-stipling-basic
nodes.description: Baseline weighted-Voronoi stippling: dots migrate toward noise-weighted cell centroids as the loop plays; cells stroked, centroids marked.
nodes.notable: The starter version of the noise-weighted Lloyd relaxation, showing both dots and their centroid targets.

nodes.name: subtractive-diffusion
nodes.description: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion on a 100x100 grid, chemical A quantized to a subtractive-color palette and drawn as filled cells
nodes.notable: Gray-Scott feed/kill params drive the pattern; color index maps chemical concentration to palette bands

nodes.name: sujni-basic
nodes.description: Sidewinder maze distance-colored into regions, each region flood-filled by nalee space-filling walkers in pipe/solid path style
nodes.notable: Sidewinder maze + BFS distance grid define color regions; PolyBool unions cells into polygons that clip separate nalee walker domains

nodes.name: sujni-basic-colors
nodes.description: Sidewinder maze distance-colored into regions filled by nalee walkers in solid style, using shuffled found-color palettes (carmen/bless)
nodes.notable: Variant of sujni-basic swapping in shuffled found-color palettes with fewer walkers

nodes.name: sujni-dither
nodes.description: Sidewinder-maze nalee fill at coarse cell size with distressed path style, then downscaled and Atkinson-dithered over the whole frame
nodes.notable: distressedStyle nalee cells plus Atkinson dither give a worn woven-cloth texture

nodes.name: sujni-dot-grid
nodes.description: Sidewinder-maze distance regions filled by nalee walkers rendered in polka-dot line style over a mindful/auto-albers palette
nodes.notable: polkaLine path style renders walker paths as dotted trails

nodes.name: sujni-gradient
nodes.description: Fixed 32x32 sidewinder maze distance-colored into regions filled by fine nalee walkers in solid style, forming a corner-to-corner gradient
nodes.notable: Start at [0,0], end at far corner so BFS distance yields a diagonal color gradient across regions

nodes.name: sujni-multiple
nodes.description: Sidewinder-maze nalee fill where each region gets a randomly chosen path style (solid, pipe, stitch, thin, polka)
nodes.notable: Mixed per-region path styles make each color patch read as a different woven stitch

nodes.name: sujni-normals
nodes.description: Small 6x6 sidewinder maze distance regions filled by nalee walkers drawn in a normals-based style over a mindful palette
nodes.notable: withNormalsStyle renders walker ribs from path normals; coarse maze yields large blocky regions

nodes.name: sujni-stitches
nodes.description: Sidewinder-maze distance regions filled by nalee walkers in stitch path style, evoking embroidered running-stitch seams
nodes.notable: stitchStyle path rendering references the sujni/kantha hand-stitch the series is named for

nodes.name: not-as-much-tau
nodes.description: Grid of squares whose size pulses via sin of a random x/y offset function over time, downscaled and Atkinson-dithered
nodes.notable: Random offset function (x-y, x*y, x/y, etc) sets the phase field driving square-size oscillation

nodes.name: tau-4
nodes.description: Grid of size-pulsing squares like not-as-much-tau but with TAU redefined to 4 instead of 2pi, retuning the wave frequency; Atkinson-dithered
nodes.notable: TAU hardcoded to 4 (not 2pi) deliberately detunes the oscillation period

nodes.name: tau-wave
nodes.description: Grid of squares displaced and resized by sin/cos of x over time across a range of TAU*TAU, then Atkinson-dithered
nodes.notable: Both position and size wobble by trig of x; grid range derived from TAU squared

nodes.name: tensors
nodes.description: EM field tensor: 320 fibonacci-sphere velocities mapped through a random antisymmetric F to Lorentz-force arrows on an orbiting sphere
nodes.notable: Picks an electric, magnetic or mixed archetype instead of 16 raw numbers, so every seed is a valid tensor with a readable field shape

nodes.name: tensors-blob
nodes.description: Pencil-stroke arrows and scribbled dots on a noise-deformed icosphere whose normals drive the EM tensor; wobbly wireframe and guide rings
nodes.notable: Reseeds the RNG every frame so the pencil jitter stays fixed while the blob loops, instead of boiling at 60fps

nodes.name: tensors-options
nodes.description: Tensor force arrows at the deduplicated vertices of a chosen three.js primitive (sphere, box, torus knot...), trackball-rotated and occluded
nodes.notable: Each vertex's normalized position is the velocity fed through the tensor, so the sphere case reproduces the original tensors sketch

nodes.name: tensors-sketch
nodes.description: Graphite take on tensors-options: wobbly wireframe of a chosen primitive, hand-jittered force arrows and faint construction circles on paper
nodes.notable: All strokes accumulate into one LineSegments buffer with per-vertex rgba, so overlapping translucent passes build up like pencil pressure

nodes.name: alt
nodes.description: Static field of horizontal wobbly ribbons built from Chaikin-smoothed polylines extruded along their normals with a tapering spread envelope
nodes.notable: Uses polyline-normals to extrude each smoothed spine into a closed lens-shaped ribbon

nodes.name: grass
nodes.description: 72 thin vertical tentacles rising from the lower canvas, each wobbling by a sum-of-sines and cast with a soft offset shadow accent, grass-like
nodes.notable: Dense count and low-amplitude spread turn the tentacle system into swaying blades of grass

nodes.name: standard
nodes.description: 12 vertical tentacles built from normal-extruded spines, each wobbling by a sum-of-sines with a translated accent layer behind
nodes.notable: Per-tentacle phase offset by index makes the group undulate out of sync

nodes.name: standard-dither
nodes.description: The standard tentacle animation with an offset accent layer, downscaled and Atkinson-dithered over the whole frame
nodes.notable: Same wobbling tentacles as standard, finished with a 0.35-scale Atkinson dither pass

nodes.name: compositions
nodes.description: Monospace ASCII/box-drawing field recursively subdivided into rectangles, each woven from weft line/density/ascii/randomart charts crossed by warp waves
nodes.notable: Weft/warp terminology treats scrolling terminal line-charts as textile; warp lines only draw over odd weft indices to fake over-under weaving

nodes.name: icons
nodes.description: Woven ascii charts: box-drawing and shaded density wefts interlaced with vertical wave warps, plus a scrolling band of logos as block glyphs
nodes.notable: The Storybook, Chromatic and GitHub marks are rasterized to a 64px coverage map and downsampled into a shade ramp so they weave under the warps

nodes.name: layered-compositions
nodes.description: Terminal-chart weave like compositions but laid out via five hand-designed modular-grid layouts (A-E) of overlapping panels instead of recursive splits
nodes.notable: Swiss-style modular layout functions place panels on a shared module grid; tweakpane rebuilds layout live

nodes.name: terminal-charts
nodes.description: Static multi-series terminal line charts (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku metrics) drawn as box-drawing glyphs with y-ticks, date labels and legends on dark ground
nodes.notable: The realistic-looking data (nice ticks, spiky/trending/flat series, month labels) is the original from which the abstract weave variants grew

nodes.name: terminal-charts-patterns
nodes.description: Full-canvas monospace weave of 18 weft line/density charts crossed by 14 warp waves, over/under masked by parity, on a random palette
nodes.notable: No rectangle framing; the whole grid is one cloth of scrolling weft rows and warp columns

nodes.name: layered-compositions
nodes.description: The terminal-charts weave laid out as a glyph-grid desktop: every chart is a draggable, resizable box-drawing window over a system bar
nodes.notable: Patterns are built in local cell coordinates, so dragging a window is free and only a resize rebuilds; the sketch fills the viewport instead of declaring dimensions

nodes.name: test
nodes.description: Cellular-automaton growth from a single center seed with von-Neumann neighbor rules, cells colored by age in cycling HSL on near-black
nodes.notable: Scratch/test file; custom growth rule (birth on exactly one active neighbor) plus age-driven hue

nodes.name: texel-colors
nodes.description: Palette proof sheet: a single texel-random display-p3 palette shown as evenly padded horizontal color strips on its background swatch
nodes.notable: Utility swatch viewer for the texel-random palette generator

nodes.name: texel-colors-basic
nodes.description: Palette comparison sheet: the texel palette generated across seven color spaces (xyz, oklab, oklch, srgb, p3, a98, rec2020) as side-by-side columns of strips
nodes.notable: Each column is the same palette rendered in a different color space to compare gamut/appearance

nodes.name: timeline-example
nodes.description: A single magenta circle animated along keyframed position and diameter tracks with mixed easings via @daeinc/timeline, on dark ground
nodes.notable: Demo of the @daeinc/timeline keyframe/easing library rather than a finished piece

nodes.name: triangle-splits
nodes.description: A random central triangle splits a square frame into a fan of seven flat-colored triangles from a mixed palette
nodes.notable: Corners of the canvas fan out to a randomly-placed interior triangle, partitioning the whole square with no gaps

nodes.name: basic
nodes.description: Stacked horizontal bands filled by trochoidal (rolling-circle) wave curves, colors from Albers palettes, animated over time
nodes.notable: Trochoidal motion (radius offset on sin) gives the wave crests a leaning, ocean-swell shape rather than a plain sine

nodes.name: dither
nodes.description: Layered trochoidal wave bands downscaled and Atkinson-dithered to a pixelated look; gamepad buttons tweak amplitude/frequency live
nodes.notable: Reads a joy-joy gamepad (X/B/Y/A) to nudge base frequency and amplitude in real time; optional grayscale ramp

nodes.name: alphabet
nodes.description: The full A-Z alphabet built from extruded pixel-font voxel columns in isometric projection via the heerich engine
nodes.notable: Bitmap font drives box extrusion; tweakpane exposes letter stretch, extrusion height, and camera controls

nodes.name: alphabet-pixel
nodes.description: A-Z alphabet from a 7-wide pixel font extruded into voxel columns, rendered in oblique projection with heerich
nodes.notable: Wider, rounder 7x9 bitmap font than the sibling alphabet sketch; oblique camera instead of isometric

nodes.name: diamond-top
nodes.description: A voxel octahedron (stacked diamond of unit cubes) rotating around Y with per-face directional shading, via heerich
nodes.notable: Layered Manhattan-radius rings form the diamond; rotation snaps to grid and dedupes voxels, faces shaded by quadrant

nodes.name: nalee
nodes.description: A single nalee space-filling walker path extruded into tall voxel columns, drawn as isometric boxes with oklch shading via heerich
nodes.notable: Bridges the nalee flow system into heerich voxels — the walker's path becomes a raised 3D ribbon of columns

nodes.name: nalee-3
nodes.description: Nalee walker path as voxel columns whose height is mapped from path length, giving a tapered isometric ribbon via heerich
nodes.notable: Column height eases from tall to short along the path length (mapRange over pts.length), so the ribbon reads as a ramp

nodes.name: nalee-p
nodes.description: Penplot variant of the nalee voxel path: white boxes with cross-hatched faces exported as an occluded A4 SVG via heerich
nodes.notable: Face hatching (per-face angle/period) plus heerich occlusion culling produce a plotter-ready line drawing on A4

nodes.name: panna-meena
nodes.description: Panna Meena ka Kund stepwell staircases rendered as interlocking oblique voxel terraces, with a back wall, via heerich
nodes.notable: Recreates the zigzag interlocking staircases of the Jaipur stepwell as tapering voxel steps in an alternating grid

nodes.name: panna-meena-p
nodes.description: Penplot version of the Panna Meena stepwell voxel terraces: black-outline white boxes exported as an occluded A4 SVG via heerich
nodes.notable: Same interlocking-staircase geometry as panna-meena but stripped to plotter line art with heerich hidden-face occlusion

nodes.name: samantha-bittman
nodes.description: A woven textile pattern of colored bands over a checkerboard ground built as a flat voxel grid in the style of Samantha Bittman, via heerich
nodes.notable: Oscillating band edges over a black/white checker mimic Bittman's hand-woven acrylic-on-textile op patterns

nodes.name: textbox
nodes.description: User-typed text extruded into voxel columns and slowly rotated around a chosen axis in orthographic projection via heerich
nodes.notable: Defaults to spelling HEERICH; tweakpane text field and X/Y/Z axis toggle drive an orthographic tumble of the word

nodes.name: todd-kelly
nodes.description: A tiled diamond height field of voxel columns with Manhattan-distance coloring and pulsing palette cycling, in the Todd Kelly palette via heerich
nodes.notable: Manhattan distance to tiled diamond centers sets both color index and column height, so the field reads as raised pyramids

nodes.name: todd-kelly-2
nodes.description: Scrolling tiled diamond voxel field (horizontal/vertical/diagonal drift) with distance-based height and color, Todd Kelly palette via heerich
nodes.notable: Randomly picks a scroll direction each run so the diamond pyramid field drifts across the plane

nodes.name: wave
nodes.description: Concentric Chebyshev-distance staircase of voxel columns whose heights cycle between bowl and dome, echoing Panna Meena stepwell, via heerich
nodes.notable: A tent wave over Chebyshev distance from center makes the terraced field breathe between a concave bowl and a convex dome

nodes.name: wallace-sewell
nodes.description: A woven textile grid of striped warp/weft blocks with random highlight bands, Atkinson-dithered, in the manner of Wallace Sewell scarves
nodes.notable: Fine tick-mark warp lines plus random highlight weft bands, then dithered, evoke Wallace Sewell woven-scarf structure

nodes.description: Wave function collapse on a 12x12 grid of box-drawing pipe and block glyphs, drawn as blue line/fill tiles
nodes.notable: Earliest WFC iteration: adjacency rules over Unicode box-drawing and half-block chars, single blue ink

nodes.description: Wave function collapse with explicit edge-typed tiles and color-group families (blue/green/orange) on a 12x12 grid
nodes.notable: Reworks WFC with connect/empty edge constraints and per-tile color groups instead of a flat rule table

nodes.description: Wave function collapse of box-drawing pipe tiles on a 24x24 grid with per-cell random palette colors over a picked background
nodes.notable: Drops the block glyphs to pure pipework; each cell carries its own palette color for a confetti-of-lines look

nodes.description: Wave function collapse pipe network on a 32x32 grid where flood-filled connected runs share one chromotome color
nodes.notable: getAllConnectedCells recolors each contiguous pipe run one color, so continuous routes read as single-hued threads

nodes.description: Botanical wave function collapse: stem/branch/leaf/curve/split tiles with curve and thickness variation grow a vine-like network on a 24x24 grid
nodes.notable: Swaps pipe glyphs for plant morphemes (stems, leaves, splits) with per-cell curve/rotation jitter for an organic, botanical WFC

nodes.description: Wave function collapse pipes drawn as arrowed lines on a 32x32 grid, connected runs sharing a color, giving a directed-flow diagram
nodes.notable: Each pipe segment gets an arrowhead, turning the WFC network into a directed graph of flows

nodes.description: Wave function collapse pipes on a dense 64x64 grid, each stroke double-drawn as a colored band cored with the background for a tube look
nodes.notable: Over-strokes each pipe with a thin bg-colored inner line so the routes read as hollow ribbon-tubes at 64x64 resolution

nodes.description: WFC over box-drawing pipe tiles (corners and straights) that connect into paths, flood-filled by connected component color, scrolling horizontally forever
nodes.notable: Colors propagate along topologically connected pipe runs, so each contiguous path reads as one hue; infinite left-scroll regenerates one collapsed column at a time

nodes.name: wobbly-grid
nodes.description: 32x32 grid of circles whose radii are driven by a summed multi-frequency sine field, drawn over a hairline grid with dark outlines
nodes.notable: The 'wobbly' function nests sines inside sines with a 45-degree rotated coordinate pair for a plaid-like breathing field

nodes.name: wobbly-grid-2
nodes.description: Variant of wobbly-grid using outlined squares instead of circles, side length modulated by the same nested multi-frequency sine field over a hairline grid
nodes.notable: Same wobbly field as wobbly-grid but mapped to square size; playhead is passed through an extra sin() giving a ping-pong rather than looping sweep

nodes.name: wobbly-wave
nodes.description: A dense row of overlapping circles traces a sine-driven wobbly band across the canvas, each circle colored by a gradient sampled along the axis
nodes.notable: Randomly picks horizontal or vertical orientation and two summed sine frequencies (a and 6-a) so each run reads differently; colors from a homegrown subtractive-color generator

nodes.name: hexagon
nodes.description: A rotating hexagon fan-filled with Bresenham lines whose pixels XOR-toggle on a 256x256 field, producing black-on-white moire interference
nodes.notable: Overlapping XOR line strokes cancel where they cross, so the solid fan dissolves into banded interference that rotates with the hexagon

nodes.name: lines
nodes.description: Static XOR field: a fan of Bresenham lines from one corner to every column top toggles pixels, yielding a black-and-white moire lattice
nodes.notable: Simplest of the xor series: a single-frame corner fan whose overlaps XOR into a periodic interference weave

nodes.name: lissajous
nodes.description: Two Lissajous curves rendered as XOR-toggled line segments on a 256x256 field, animating into shifting white-on-black interference figures
nodes.notable: Chords span a spread of Lissajous phase offsets and XOR against each other, so the harmonic figure appears as negative-space bands rather than a drawn line

nodes.name: lissajous-pack
nodes.description: Circle-packed field of many Lissajous figures at varied scales, each drawn as XOR-toggled line chords, animating as white-on-black interference clusters
nodes.notable: pack-spheres lays out up to 50 Lissajous cells with phase offsets keyed to index, so each packed disc animates its own harmonic pattern

nodes.name: lissajous-rgb
nodes.description: Three phase-shifted Lissajous figures each tagged red, green, or blue write into a shared XOR field, producing overlapping additive-primary interference
nodes.notable: Each channel's XOR overwrites the cell value with its own index, so RGB primaries compete for pixels rather than blending, giving hard-edged color separation

nodes.name: polar-shape
nodes.description: A rotating 12-sided polygon fan-filled with XOR lines, then per-column pixel shifting displaces alternating columns for a glitched moire
nodes.notable: After the XOR fan renders, each column's pixels shift left or right by parity and frame, smearing the interference into a scanline-like displacement

nodes.name: polar-shape-shift
nodes.description: A 12-sided polygon fan-filled with XOR lines whose center travels across the canvas as it rotates, dragging the interference pattern with it
nodes.notable: Center x is driven by playhead so the rotating polygon sweeps left-to-right, its moire fan moving like a traveling wavefront

nodes.name: triangle
nodes.description: A rotating triangle fan-filled with XOR-toggled Bresenham lines on a 256x256 field, dissolving the solid triangle into black-and-white moire
nodes.notable: Only vertex 0's fan of 50 lines is drawn, so the triangle fills as a single-corner sweep whose XOR overlaps read as concentric interference

clusters.name: The Nalee System
clusters.blurb: The homegrown negative-space engine: a domain is packed with lines, ribbons, and arcs that leave the ground showing through. Every variant re-tunes the same generative rule for filling a shape while preserving emptiness.

clusters.name: Weaving and Thread
clusters.blurb: Work that thinks like a loom — warp-and-weft grids, stitched marks, and interlaced color drawn from sujni quilts and the Bauhaus weavers. Structure is built up thread by thread rather than composed.

clusters.name: Hulls and Aggregates
clusters.blurb: Scattered points bound into shape: convex hulls stretched around clusters like rubber bands, poisson-packed dots, and stippled fields. The image is the aggregate, not the individual mark.

clusters.name: Tiling and Truchet
clusters.blurb: A single unit tile repeated and rotated across a grid until pattern emerges — Truchet arcs, Wang tiles, and modular toy-part motifs. Order comes from the rule that joins one cell to the next.

clusters.name: Moire and Op Art
clusters.blurb: Optical vibration from interference: XOR lattices, wobbling grids, and superimposed line rasters that flicker and beat. The subject is the eye's response, not the geometry itself.

clusters.name: Subdivided Grids
clusters.blurb: The plane recursively cut into rectangles, cells, and triangles. Each piece inherits and distorts its parent, so the finished image is a record of the partitioning process.

clusters.name: Concrete Art
clusters.blurb: Hard-edge homages to the concrete and constructivist tradition — Albers, Bill, Kelly, Swain, van den Berg. Flat planes of color arranged by system and chance rather than by hand.

clusters.name: Color Studies and Gradients
clusters.blurb: Direct investigations of color itself: gradient ramps, banded fractions, and palette instruments. Form is kept plain so the relationships between hues carry the work.

clusters.name: Architectural Space
clusters.blurb: Built space on the flat page — isometric voxels, raycast rooms, perspective windows, and Heerich-like structures. Depth is asserted through projection while the surface stays graphic.

clusters.name: Simulation and Physics
clusters.blurb: Agents and forces left to run: boids, slime, spring-and-verlet bodies, growth by accretion, colliding polygons. The drawing is the residue of a process unfolding in time.

clusters.name: Emergent Grids and Automata
clusters.blurb: Discrete state evolving cell by cell — cellular automata, wave-function collapse, reaction-diffusion. Simple local rules are iterated until global pattern appears.

clusters.name: Fields, Flows and Waves
clusters.blurb: Continuous fields made visible: flow lines, trig and trochoidal waves, chladni nodes, and conformal distortions of the grid. Marks follow an underlying vector or potential.

clusters.name: ASCII and Terminal
clusters.blurb: Images rendered in monospace glyphs and terminal type — maze distance fields, charts, and a self-printing quine. Text becomes texture and the character grid becomes the canvas.

threads.name: The Nalee System, End to End
threads.note: The negative-space packing rule from its birth as a sujni quilt through Kelly awnings, a detour into physarum trails, hull and jali variants, and its late migration into single-line and voxel forms.

threads.name: Rubber Bands and Hulls
threads.note: Convex hulls as a recurring device — from early clustered slashes and shattered polygons to colliding shells, nalee hulls, and the rubber-band-stipple series where the hull becomes an elastic band snapped around dots.

threads.name: Textile Logic
threads.note: The loom as a mental model, developing from embroidered spirals and sujni stitches through Albers weavings, a soft-body rug, clearloop and anni-weaving, and finally woven terminal charts and rubber-band stipple.

threads.name: Dithering as a Treatment
threads.note: A halftone finish returning across unrelated systems — patchwork, sujni, growth, physarum, cluster growth, tau waves, curve particles, and fractal grids all resolved through the same dot screen.

threads.name: Optical Vibration
threads.note: The pursuit of flicker and moire — wobbling grids and mobius bands giving way to tau waves, snowflakes, gravura blinds, XOR lattices, and optical voxel weaves.

threads.name: Windows, Screens and Blinds
threads.note: The aperture as a recurring form — perspective windows and khidki lattices, jali screens, distorted domain-polygon windows, nalee jali, and gravura blinds that slide open and shut.

threads.name: Text as Image
threads.note: Rendering into the character grid — from maze distance fields and cluster-growth printouts to a console color traveller, chladni type, a quine, and the terminal-charts series.

threads.name: Process as Image
threads.note: Simulations left to draw themselves — boids and DLA growth, physarum trails, wave-function collapse, soft bodies, flowing curve particles, and XOR automata, each image the trace of a run.

insights.title: Drive nalee walkers with a distance field
insights.body: nalee's 73 sketches route and color by grid occupancy, flow fields and polar grids, but never by a distance field — yet maze-distance builds gorgeous shells by shading cells by their geodesic distance, and the voxels/heerich work already uses distance-field height. Compute a distance transform over a nalee domain (from a seed, an edge, or a clipping polygon) and key ribbon color, width, or spawn priority to it, importing the maze-distance falloff into the space-filling engine.

insights.title: Give the XOR interference field a palette
insights.body: The eight-sketch xor series is locked to black-and-white; only lissajous-rgb hints at more, writing three phase-shifted fields into R, G and B channels. Meanwhile snowflake already has a clean recipe for turning a scalar field into color bands: floor(dist^scale) mod palette. Transfer it — index a palette LUT by the XOR accumulation count instead of thresholding to one bit — and the moiré interference becomes tonal color banding while keeping the hard optical vibration intact.

insights.title: Plot the nalee walker as a printed suite
insights.body: Nalee is the studio's signature object (73 sketches) but meets the pen plotter in only a handful of 2026 experiments (voxels/nalee-p, the two heerich plots) — four penplot sketches total. The single-line Hamiltonian meander (nalee-one-line/basic, albers-meander) is the ideal candidate: a Warnsdorff path draws as one continuous pen stroke with zero pen-ups, so it can go straight into src/penplot/render-penplot.ts as a true single-stroke drawing. Commit a coherent A4 plotter suite — the one-line meander, the k_best overlapping-hull composition, and a clipped Kelly region — sized and occluded for physical output, and extend the same treatment to nalee-hulls and conformal-mapping/nalee.

insights.title: Sample the sparse end of nalee
insights.body: Across 73 nalee sketches only 10 read as sparse; the engine is almost always run dense or medium, so its behavior at low walker counts and large cells is under-explored. Deliberately run nalee with a handful of walkers on a coarse grid so individual ribbons become discrete specific objects with negative space around them, the opposite of the usual all-over fill.

insights.title: Weave a real loom draft through nalee ribbons
insights.body: anni-weaving encodes genuine weave drafts — twill, herringbone, satin, monk's belt — as over/under warp/weft masks, while nalee's ribbons only evoke weaving (the weaving-structure concept spans 47 sketches without ever actually interlacing). Combine them: use a weave draft as the parity mask that decides which nalee walker ribbon passes over and which passes under at each crossing. The two textile threads that have run in parallel since 2024 finally become one genuinely woven object.

insights.title: Feed the SAT packing engine to the tilers
insights.body: The collision series runs a proper SAT/convex-hull physics packer, but its settled arrangements of convex shapes are never used as input to any tiling or fill system — they just demonstrate collision. Take a packed collision layout and hand its cells to nalee (as domains), heerich (as isometric footprints), or map-maker, so physics discovers the partition that a systematic fill then inhabits.

insights.title: Push the overlapping-hull nalee system past its keeper
insights.body: nalee-hulls/k_best is the artist's own selected keeper — overlapping Poisson convex hulls filled with nalee, foreground and background color sets split by WCAG contrast — and i, j, l push the overlap counts higher. All twelve were made in a single day (Sept 2025) and the series stopped exactly at its strongest piece. Take k_best further: many more overlapping hulls at a larger scale, or the same composition rendered for large-format print where the contrast-split reads as flat Kelly planes.

insights.title: Forms that exist only as their overlaps
insights.body: siep-van-den-berg/no-251 makes black rectangles on black that are visible solely where they intersect (white) or triple-overlap (grey), and boolean/robert-swain repaints overlaps in inverted color — a pure ‘figure = intersection’ idea that got two or three pieces and stopped. The clipped sliding-blind work (development-of-concrete-art/fibonacci-blinds, op-art/grid) is the same negative-space logic in motion. Deepen it into a series where the source rectangles are never drawn at all, only their boolean regions, animated as the shapes slide across a Swain palette so the visible field is entirely emergent.

insights.title: Extrude Kelly color fields into voxel relief
insights.body: The voxels series (13 sketches, all 2026, via the heerich isometric engine) is mostly monochrome and architectural — stepwells, alphabets — and only voxels/nalee extrudes a walker path. Separately, anni-weaving/heerich-depth already proves the engine can raise one cell class and keep another flat as a relief. Combine them: extrude the kelly-nalee color-field compositions so each nalee-filled Kelly region becomes raised or flat voxel terrain, giving the hard-edge color blocks physical depth without leaving the flat-file palette.

insights.title: Clip every system to a jali screen, not just nalee
insights.body: clipping-mask is nalee's most-used technique (40 sketches) and the jali perforated-screen domain exists in nalee-jali and jali/truchet, but the jali clip has only ever masked nalee walks and one truchet tiling. Reuse clipDomainWithWorldCoords from nalee/domain.ts to clip domain-polygon subdivisions, heerich voxel stacks, and clixo tilings to a jali lattice, letting a second system show through the screen's holes.

insights.title: Make snowflake's distance-power-modulo a series
insights.body: Only two sketches, a year apart, explore the floor(dist^scale) mod palette rule (snowflake, then snowflake/16x16 which retiles it at escalating exponents) — a genuinely clean specific-object system that concentric-square-bands a dot grid. It never became a series. Vary the one thing that matters: swap the Euclidean metric for Manhattan and Chebyshev (as voxels/todd-kelly already does for heights), change the modulo base, and animate the exponent alone so the banding breathes without any other motion.

insights.title: Push systems other than nalee through the conformal and bipolar maps
insights.body: conformal-mapping/nalee already warps nalee walker paths through sin(z) and proves the warp composes cleanly onto a real system — but only nalee ever gets warped, even though the transforms catalogue has z², 1/z, exp and ln ready and bipolar adds spiral/lens space. Push a different rigid orthogonal system through the same maps: the anni-weaving weave grid, the xor interference field, the Wang-tile quilt, heerich's isometric voxel lattice, or clixo's tile grid, applying the conformal/bipolar domainToWorld to their cell positions. Systematic distortion of an already-gridded object reads very differently on a woven, moiré, or isometric source.

insights.title: Stippling returned without its voronoi engine
insights.body: stipling-noise (2024) built stippling on a voronoi + Lloyd-relaxation core, but the 15-sketch rubber-band-stipple revival (2026) rebuilt point distribution from poisson-disk and convex hulls and dropped voronoi/Lloyd entirely — a capable relaxation engine left on the shelf. Reintroduce Lloyd relaxation into rubber-band-stipple so the stipple points settle into even, organic spacing, or use the voronoi cells themselves as the woven regions.

insights.title: Dither the flat domain-polygon and nalee fields
insights.body: Dithering is a first-class utility here (src/dither.ts) and carries cluster-growth, curve-particles and gravura, but domain-polygon uses it zero times and nalee only twice across 73 sketches — both systems output large flat color areas that are exactly what an ordered/error-diffusion dither transforms. Run domain-polygon's subdivided regions and nalee's ribbons through the existing dither pass to add tonal grain and gradient banding without changing the geometry.

insights.title: Build tonal-monochrome twins of the loud series
insights.body: curve-particles lives entirely in chromotome color with Atkinson dithering, and quantum-equivalence and gravura only ever appear saturated — yet the record's quietest, strongest pieces are tonal monochrome (black-on-black's near-black P3 greys, gears, grey-goo). Make the missing twin: run curve-particles' dithered particle-and-mesh system in near-black tonal greys like black-on-black, so the same anti-compositional flow field yields a hushed grisaille object instead of a bright one.

insights.title: Compose the raycasting silhouettes without a mouse
insights.body: raycasting/circles and raycasting/solid cut the lit visibility polygon out of a black shadow layer with destination-out — light reveals the ground as a calm, minimal negative shape, exactly the quiet register PRODUCT.md wants. But all four raycasting pieces are interactive, tied to a following mouse, so they never resolve into a fixed image. Move the emitter by rule instead of cursor and render static, composed silhouettes; the strongest image here is one nobody can currently see standing still.

insights.title: A dedicated Robert Swain color-field series
insights.body: Robert Swain shows up four times — boolean/robert-swain, clearloop/robert-swain, clearloop/robert-swain-lights-on-off, and echoed in spectrum-colors-arranged-by-chance — but always as a borrowed palette, never as its own object. Swain's actual practice is the systematic color-gradient grid across a full hue wheel. Build the series he implies: the 40x40 chance-placed RYB grid of rybitten-blinds resolved into an ordered 30-step hue-by-value lattice, one specific color object per canvas.

insights.title: Formalize the diagrammatic-instrument register
insights.body: A mock-technical-drawing voice keeps surfacing unplanned: rubber-banding/micro-graphics frames the band as a HUD, rubber-band-stipple/weaving-techniques as a pulley schematic, terminal-charts as box-drawing plots, memory-leak as a fake cartridge, quine as its own scrolling source. Each is a specific object that happens to look like an instrument. Make it deliberate — a series of ‘instruments’ where the generative geometry is rendered as its own annotated technical drawing (tick marks, tangent construction lines, counters) so the diagram is the object, not an explanation of one.

insights.title: Turn the dry-brush field stroke into a study
insights.body: electric-field/gradient-paint renders flux lines as multi-bristle dry-brush strokes — a painterly, gestural texture that appears essentially nowhere else in a record dominated by hard-edge, flat shapes (198 hard-edge vs a handful of soft). It's a genuine outlier worth interrogating rather than leaving as a one-off. Apply the same multi-bristle stroke to the other vector and trail fields — physarum trails, curve-particles, chladni trails — as a deliberate 'brushed field' study to see whether the studio has a quiet painterly register at all.

insights.title: Cross xor/moire with a named grid system
insights.body: The xor series (eight sketches, Jan 2026) generates moire and XOR interference on its own bespoke grid and never touches any engine; nalee, heerich and clixo all maintain exactly the regular lattices XOR patterns need. Compute an xor-pattern field over a nalee grid domain or a heerich isometric lattice and use it to gate cell fill or ribbon color, marrying the interference look to a real spatial system.

insights.title: Wire the abandoned adjacency solvers into clixo and nalee
insights.body: paint-without-thinking built a full Wang/truchet adjacency solver (all ten sketches dated 2025-09-26) and wave-function-collapse built an adjacency-constraint solver (eight variants, one day, 2024-11-27) — neither has driven a layout since, while clixo and quantum-equivalence still tile by hand. Repurpose one solver as the placement brain: let it drive clixo's tile selection, seed a nalee sub-domain layout, or place paint-without-thinking's own tile set, so collapse and adjacency constraints replace hand-tuned modulo and random placement.

insights.title: Return to the Wang-tile 'paint without thinking' at density
insights.body: The ten-sketch burst of paint-without-thinking (all one day, Sept 2025) grows edge-matched arc and triangle Wang tiles into flat color areas — the most rigorously anti-compositional system in the whole record, arrangements discovered entirely by tile-matching. arcs-reduction-rounded is the quilt-like keeper. It never came back. Revisit it as a printed suite and add the scale it lacks: a full-bleed field of hundreds of tiny arc tiles rather than a 3x3 grid, where the found composition emerges at density.

insights.title: Feed the archive back into itself
insights.body: color-traveller/color-traveller-images literally feeds the sketchbook's own dated PNG exports back in as source frames and cross-fades them; quine scrolls its own source; disco-color-fractions/console draws into the devtools console. process-as-image is the fourth-largest concept (92 sketches), yet self-reference is a one-off every time. Pursue it as a series that renders the record itself — morph a day's outputs into each other, or pack a year of archive thumbnails into a single generated field — turning the archive into material.

insights.title: Port the CPU field-sims onto the idle WebGPU harness
insights.body: 367 of 372 catalogued sketches are canvas2d, yet a working WebGPU stack (Clifford attractors, raymarch, GPU particles, GPU reaction-diffusion) sits in src/shader-sketches and never enters the archive. The catalogued physarum trail-sim, chladni plate, boids flock, verlet soft-bodies and subtractive-diffusion are all O(n^2) or per-pixel iterative and CPU-bound — reimplement one on the existing wgpu compute harness to unlock resolutions and step counts the canvas versions can't reach.
